title: Coherent modules on a locally Noetherian scheme: kernels, cokernels, sums, quasi-coherent sub- and quotient modules
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with its kernels (sectionwise) and cokernels (sheafified sectionwise quotients). (1) If $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], then $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ are coherent; if $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are coherent, so is $\mathcal F\oplus\mathcal G$. (2) If $\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module, then $\mathcal F'$ and the quotient $\mathcal F/\mathcal F'$ (the cokernel of the inclusion) are coherent.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y0 (lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian, line 2310: kernel and cokernel of a map of coherent modules are coherent, any extension of coherent sheaves is coherent; restatement of Modules, Lemma 01BY, modules-lemma-coherent-abelian) and Lemma 01Y1 (lemma-coherent-Noetherian-quasi-coherent-sub-quotient, line 2329)

proof.text: Work on an affine open U = Spec(A) of the locally Noetherian scheme X. The restriction of a quasi-coherent module to U is quasi-coherent, and [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] identifies coherence on U with quasi-coherence plus finite type. Thus coherent F and G have finitely generated section modules F(U) and G(U) by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. The same affine description computes kernels and cokernels of maps of quasi-coherent modules on U, by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y0 (tag 01Y0, line 2310), reduced to affine opens using Properties Lemma 01XZ (tag 01XZ) and Modules Lemma 01IC (tag 01IC)

proof.text: On U, the kernel is a submodule of the finitely generated A-module F(U), and the cokernel is a quotient of the finitely generated A-module G(U). Since A is Noetherian, the finite-module Noetherian result [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc] implies that the kernel submodule is finitely generated; the quotient is finitely generated by the images of a finite generating set. The quasi-coherence from Step 1 therefore makes both kernel and cokernel coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The direct sum F plus G is quasi-coherent and its affine sections are F(U) plus G(U), generated by the union of two finite generating sets, so it is coherent by the same criterion. This is the affine calculation in Stacks 01Y0, glued over affine neighbourhoods.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y0 (tag 01Y0), using Modules Lemma 01BY (coherent modules form an abelian category) and the affine proof of its kernel/cokernel closure

proof.text: Let F' be a quasi-coherent submodule of coherent F. On every affine Noetherian U = Spec(A), F(U) is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], while F'(U) is an A-submodule of F(U); hence F'(U) is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc]. The inclusion has quasi-coherent cokernel by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], and its sections are the quotient F(U)/F'(U), which is finitely generated. Thus F' and F/F' are quasi-coherent of finite type and therefore coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. This is the local argument of Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 01Y1.

split_report.summary: Split along Cohomology of Schemes Lemmas 01Y0 and 01Y1. Three steps reduce to affine opens of a locally Noetherian scheme, use the coherent iff quasi-coherent finite-type criterion and the existing quasi-coherent kernel/cokernel computations, then apply Noetherian finite-module closure to obtain finite type for kernels, cokernels, direct sums, and quasi-coherent submodules and quotients. All reusable ingredients are existing DAG nodes; no private proof lemma or new child node was introduced. The item’s recorded LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, and Mathlib grep audits correctly find no coherent-sheaf closure theorem in Mathlib.
